question: Why does this program print 5 instead of 6?
options: Because increment() was never actually called
Because C requires a return statement to update num
Because C passes arguments by value, so x inside increment() is a separate copy, and modifying it does not affect the caller's num
explanation: C passes function arguments by value by default — increment() receives a copy of num in its local variable x, so changes to x have no effect on the original num back in main().
